title: Viradha
hook: a roar in the deep forest, and something huge snatches Sita before anyone can draw a bow

segments.voice: Yesterday: the sages, part three. They hosted Rama with water, a seat and food, and at sunrise he walked into the deep forest. Did you offer someone a seat first? Today the week closes, with the first danger of the forest. Day five hundred fifty-three.

The noise comes first: a roar that shakes the trees. Then the shape, as tall as a hill, with a gaping mouth and a huge iron spear, and on the spear, Valmiki says, hang the bodies of the animals he has killed, lions and tigers and deer. His name is Viradha. Before Rama or Lakshmana can move, he grabs Sita, lifts her up, and steps back, holding her. Then he speaks, and he laughs at them.
screen: `A ROAR THAT SHAKES THE TREES.` → `A SPEAR HUNG WITH ANIMALS.` → `HE GRABS SITA.`

segments.voice: Viradha mocks them. You look like ascetics, he says, with your bark and your matted hair, but you carry bows and you have a woman with you. What kind of hermits are you? She'll be my wife now. And he says something else: Brahma gave me a boon. No weapon can kill me. Rama's first response is grief. He turns to Lakshmana, stricken, and says that seeing Sita in a stranger's grip hurts more than his father's death, more than losing the kingdom. It's Lakshmana, furious, who pulls him back into the moment. Then both brothers shoot. Arrows strike Viradha again and again and don't kill him. He drops Sita, seizes the two brothers, swings them onto his shoulders like children, and runs off into the forest. Sita is left screaming after them. And the brothers, carried along, do the only thing left. They break his arms. Rama the right, Lakshmana the left. Viradha falls. Now the week. Bharata on the road, suspected at every stop. A pair of sandals stepped into on Chitrakoot. A throne at Nandigrama with no king on it, and Anasuya's gifts to Sita. The sages of Dandaka, asking for a protector. The four stages of life and the heat of tapas. A guest welcomed as a god. And today, the welcome ends, and the forest shows its teeth.
screen: `WHAT KIND OF HERMITS ARE YOU?` · `NO WEAPON CAN KILL ME.` · `CARRIED OFF ON HIS SHOULDERS.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `THE FOREST SHOWS ITS TEETH.`

segments.voice: Sit and notice your breath. Think of a moment when something sudden happened, a shock, a bad phone call, a near miss, and you froze before you could act. Let the memory be there without replaying it. Notice where your body tightened then. Now let a slow breath reach that spot. Rama froze in grief, and his brother brought him back. Imagine someone you trust saying your name, steady, calling you back into the room. The bell holds the time.
Viradha. The forest giant who seizes Sita, mocks the brothers as false hermits, and can't be killed by weapons.
Your line: no weapon can kill me. Today, if someone near you freezes in a hard moment, say their name gently and stay close. Day five hundred fifty-three.

screen: `DAY 553 COUNTS.` → `A WEEK FROM CHITRAKOOT INTO THE WILD, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: VIRADHA, PART TWO.`

howItsDone: Viradha is the first danger Rama meets in the Aranya Kanda, and reciters linger on Rama's grief when Sita is seized.

original.note: Sanskrit virādha: the name of the forest giant Rama meets first in the Aranya Kanda.

trapdoor: what you thought: Viradha is just a monster in the woods.
what it means: he's protected by a boon, and he mocks Rama's whole way of life.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 2–4 make Viradha the forest's first test, and some readers hear his question, why do hermits carry bows, again later in Sita's own words.
recall: one who shoots at a sound

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Aranya Kanda 2–4 (Viradha seizes Sita; the boon; the fight; the broken arms)
